title: Elodie and the Witness
premise: True-crime podcaster Ines Oyelaran, famous for unmasking three 'accidents' as murders, receives a retainer from a nervous stranger named Corin Ash to prove that a woman named Elodie Voss has not yet been killed — a prediction, not a cold case. Digging into the coastal town of Marrow Bay, Ines discovers Elodie is the sole witness to a decades-old cover-up involving the town's founding families, and that everyone who could identify her insists she died years ago. As Ines closes in on the living witness hiding in plain sight, she realizes her client isn't trying to prevent the murder but to control when it happens, forcing her to choose between exposing the truth and protecting the fragile found family Elodie has built around a false identity. In the end, Ines broadcasts the testimony live before the killers can silence it, saving Elodie at the cost of her own career and safety.
about_author: Ivo Vane is the pen name of a former court reporter who spent eleven years transcribing small-town trials before turning to fiction. They write mysteries about people who know too much and say too little.

chapters.title: The Retainer
chapters.summary: Ines Oyelaran, riding high after solving her third 'accident,' meets a pale, precise stranger named Corin Ash who pays double to prove a murder hasn't happened yet — to a woman already declared dead. Ines's POV. The beat is wary fascination: the case is impossible, and impossible is her brand.

chapters.title: Marrow Bay
chapters.summary: Ines drives to the fog-bound coastal town where Elodie Voss supposedly drowned in 1998. The records office burns conveniently the night she arrives. Ines's POV. Emotional beat: the first prickle of being watched, of a town closing like a hand.

chapters.title: Everyone Loved Her, No One Knew Her
chapters.summary: Ines interviews townsfolk who describe Elodie warmly but contradict each other on everything — hair, age, even the drowning itself. A diner waitress, Sefa, slips her a matchbook with a phone number. Ines's POV. Beat: unease sharpening into certainty that the town is rehearsed.

chapters.title: The Voice on the Line
chapters.summary: The matchbook number reaches a woman who says only: 'Stop looking, or she dies sooner.' Ines traces the call to a shuttered cannery. Alternating with Corin's POV, who monitors her progress with unsettling calm. Beat: dread — the prediction is being managed.

chapters.title: Three Accidents, Revisited
chapters.summary: Ines maps her three solved cases against Marrow Bay and finds each victim once worked for the Halloway family, the town's founders. Her producer, Dev, urges her to drop it. Ines's POV. Beat: ambition curdling into obligation — this pattern chose her, not the reverse.

chapters.title: Corin's Ledger
chapters.summary: Corin's POV chapter: he reviews payments to six townspeople, noting which have begun to fail their instructions. He is revealed to be protecting something, not merely predicting. Beat: chilling ambiguity — his tenderness toward Elodie is real, and terrible.

chapters.title: The Woman at the Lighthouse
chapters.summary: Following the cannery lead, Ines finds an off-grid community led by a matriarch, Birdie, who feeds her soup and lies beautifully. A teenage girl, Nell, stares at Ines like she recognizes her. Ines's POV. Beat: warmth with teeth — found family as camouflage.

chapters.title: Dead Girl Walking
chapters.summary: Nell secretly leads Ines to a hidden room: Elodie Voss is alive, middle-aged, going by another name, protected by the community for twenty-five years. Elodie refuses to testify. Ines's POV. Beat: triumph immediately complicated by Elodie's terror and dignity.

chapters.title: What Elodie Saw
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV: flashbacks to 1998, when she witnessed the Halloways drown a whistleblower and was smuggled out by a young Corin Ash. She explains why silence bought twenty-five lives. Beat: grief and moral weight — survival has cost her every version of herself.

chapters.title: A Leak in the Family
chapters.summary: Someone in the lighthouse community has been feeding Corin updates. Nell goes missing overnight. Ines suspects Birdie's son Tomas. Ines's POV. Beat: betrayal inside sanctuary; loyalty begins cracking along its fault lines.

chapters.title: The Producer's Dilemma
chapters.summary: Dev arrives unannounced, having been contacted by a Halloway lawyer offering Ines a lucrative exclusive — if she kills the story. Ines refuses; Dev wavers. Dual POV. Beat: the price of truth made literal, friendship strained by money.

chapters.title: Ashes of the Record
chapters.summary: Ines's apartment and studio are ransacked; her archived episodes are wiped from every platform within hours. Only Dev's backup drive survives. Ines's POV. Beat: isolation — the machinery of the cover-up extends further than one town.

chapters.title: Tomas Confesses
chapters.summary: Cornered, Tomas admits he reported to Corin — but claims he did it to keep the payments flowing that fund the community's clinic and school. Ines's POV. Beat: moral vertigo; the traitor was paying the rent on everyone's safety.

chapters.title: Corin's Bargain
chapters.summary: Corin finally meets Ines face to face: he reveals the Halloway heir, Marcus, has discovered Elodie lives and hired him to deliver her — a job Corin intends to botch. He needs Ines to move her first. Corin's POV. Beat: uneasy alliance between two liars with aligned interests.

chapters.title: Moving Day
chapters.summary: The evacuation plan goes wrong when Marcus's men hit the lighthouse road early. Birdie is injured covering the retreat; Nell returns, having been held as leverage. Ines's POV. Beat: fear and fury — the found family bleeds for a secret that was never theirs.

chapters.title: Nell's Choice
chapters.summary: Nell's POV: she escaped her captors by promising Marcus she'd deliver Elodie herself, buying time. Torn between the only mother she's known and the town that raised her, she chooses to double-cross both. Beat: coming-of-age under fire; loyalty redefined as action, not obedience.

chapters.title: The Cannery Standoff
chapters.summary: Ines, Elodie, Corin, and Nell barricade in the cannery as Marcus's men close in. Corin takes a bullet meant for Elodie. Ines's POV. Beat: siege tension; the man who sold her protection now spends it.

chapters.title: Live From Marrow Bay
chapters.summary: With signal fading and doors failing, Ines does the reckless thing: streams Elodie's full testimony live to her dormant feed, which Dev resurrects from the backup drive. Thousands listen as Marcus's men break in. Ines's POV. Beat: climax — truth as a weapon fired in real time.

chapters.title: What the Microphone Caught
chapters.summary: The broadcast ends mid-struggle. State police, tipped by listeners nationwide, flood Marrow Bay and arrest Marcus Halloway and two deputies complicit since 1998. Ines's POV, disoriented and bruised. Beat: breathless aftermath — the audience became the witness.

chapters.title: The Cost of the Story
chapters.summary: Ines faces legal exposure for the livestream and learns her network has dropped her; sponsors flee. Dev stands by her anyway. Ines's POV. Beat: bittersweet reckoning — she saved Elodie and lost the career built on other people's graves.

chapters.title: Birdie's Table
chapters.summary: Weeks later, Elodie chooses to reclaim her name publicly; the community gathers at Birdie's table, Tomas forgiven but not forgotten, Corin recovering under watchful eyes. Elodie's POV. Beat: quiet restoration — identity returned, family chosen and kept.

chapters.title: Episode One Hundred
chapters.summary: Independent now, Ines records her hundredth episode from a rented room: Elodie's story, told with her consent, ending not with a killer caught but with a life given back. A new listener email arrives — another impossible case. Ines's POV. Beat: resolution with an open door; the price was paid, and she'd pay again.
